title: Marked invariant algebras descend to a polynomial cylinder
statement:
Let $V$ be a field or a complete discrete valuation ring, let $r\geq1$, and let $B$ be a complete Noetherian normal local domain. Suppose $V\subseteq B$ is a coefficient subring inducing an isomorphism on residue fields and there is an injective module-finite local map $V[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]\to B$. Let a finite group $H$, of order invertible in $V$, act by local automorphisms on $B$ and on $V$, compatibly with this map and fixing each variable. If $V$ is a field, assume $H$ is trivial. Assume that $\Lambda=V^H$ is a field or a complete discrete valuation ring respectively. Assume also that for some $f\in V[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ with nonzero reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_V$, the finite map is etale after inverting $f$. Set $A_0=B^H$. Given any finite family of ideals $I_1,\ldots,I_s\subseteq A_0$, there exist an $H$-equivariant change of formal coordinates $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ fixing $V$, the complete coefficient ring $D=\Lambda[[u_1,\ldots,u_{r-1}]]$, a finite type $D[T]$-algebra $C$, a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset C$ lying over $(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, and ideals $J_1,\ldots,J_s\subseteq C$ with an isomorphism
$$\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0$$
as $D$-algebras, carrying $J_i\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}$ onto $I_i$. The map $D\to A_0$ here is the inclusion defined by the invariant formal coordinates. The ring map $D[T]\to C$ is quasi-finite: it is finite type and its fibres are finite spectra with finite residue-field extensions. The residue field $C/\mathfrak n$ is finite over $D/\mathfrak m_D$. If $s=0$ the same assertion holds without ideals; the ideals $0$ and $A_0$ are allowed.

Normal means integrally closed domain, and the fixed subring consists of elements fixed by every element of $H$. Use [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] for the indicated ring notions. The hat denotes completion for powers of the maximal ideal of the specified local ring.

source.place: V 2.2.1--2.2.8 and 3.2.2--3.2.4, pp.65--68: Weierstrass change of coordinates, Elkik descent to the henselian cylinder, descent of primary ideals, then finite-presentation descent to a pointed etale neighbourhood of the polynomial cylinder. The quasi-finite map is the composite of a finite algebra and that etale neighbourhood. This formulation takes the equivariant finite formal presentation as a hypothesis; it does not construct a cover of an arbitrary complete local ring.

proof.text: The element $1/|H|$ has trace one. Apply [lem-per-trace-one-noetherian-invariant-finiteness] to $V$ and to $B$: $V$ is finite over $\Lambda$, and $A_0=B^H$ is Noetherian. The ring $A_0$ is local: an invariant element outside $\mathfrak m_B$ has invariant inverse. It is a normal domain: an element of $\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$ integral over $A_0$ lies in $B$ by normality of $B$, and is fixed by $H$, hence lies in $A_0$. Set $R_\Lambda=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. The formal-ring finiteness clause of [lem-per-finite-coefficient-henselian-cylinder], applied with $e=r-1$ and $T=t_r$, makes $V[[t]]$ finite over $R_\Lambda$. Thus $B$ is finite over $R_\Lambda$. This ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], so its submodule $A_0\subset B$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite].

By [lem-per-noetherian-primary-decomposition], write each marking as a finite intersection of primary ideals $Q$. For $I_i=A_0$ use the empty intersection. Keep $Q=0$ separately; it already descends as the zero ideal of every model. For every remaining $Q$, [lem-per-normal-finite-primary-dichotomy] gives either $g_Q\in Q\cap R_\Lambda$ with nonzero reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, or, in the DVR case, $Q=P^{(n)}$ with $P$ a height-one prime containing a fixed uniformizer $\pi\in\Lambda$. All its hypotheses were established in step 1. Call the first list the scalar-annihilated components and the second the vertical components.

Replace the ramification denominator $f$ by its norm $F_0=\prod_{h\in H}h(f)$. It lies in $R_\Lambda$: fixed power series have fixed coefficients, and $H$ fixes all variables. Its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_V$ is a product of nonzero series, hence nonzero; since $\mathfrak m_V\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, its reduction over $\Lambda$ is nonzero. Inverting $F_0$ also inverts $f$. Multiply $F_0$, all the finitely many $g_Q$, and $t_r$ to form $F\in\mathfrak m_{R_\Lambda}$, still nonzero modulo $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$. Apply [lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder] to $F$. The shear substitutions $t_i\mapsto t_i+t_r^{N_i}$ have coefficients in $\Lambda$ and commute with $H$. Equivalently use their inverse to choose formal coordinates $u_i$, with $T=u_r$, in which $F$ is a unit times a distinguished polynomial $g\in D[T]$ of positive degree, where $D=\Lambda[[u_1,\ldots,u_{r-1}]]$. Set $R=D[[T]]$ and $S=(D[T]_{(\mathfrak m_D,T)})^h$. The cited node identifies $R$ with both completions of $S$.

Put $E=V[[u_1,\ldots,u_{r-1}]]$, $S_V=(E[T]_{(\mathfrak m_E,T)})^h$, and $R_V=E[[T]]$. Apply [lem-per-finite-coefficient-henselian-cylinder]: $S_V$ is finite local over $S$, $S$ is excellent, $(S_V,gS_V)$ is henselian, its $g$-adic completion is $R_V$, and $R\otimes_S S_V\cong R_V$. Each coefficient automorphism of $V$ extends to $S_V$ by the unique local henselian extension; this gives its $H$-action and fixes $S$ and $g$. The finite $R_V$-algebra $B$ is etale away from $g$, since $F$ is a multiple of $f$ and a unit times $g$. Apply [lem-per-elkik-finite-etale-away-completion] to the Noetherian henselian pair $(S_V,gS_V)$. Obtain a finite $S_V$-algebra $\widetilde B$, etale away from $g$, with $R_V\otimes_{S_V}\widetilde B\cong B$.

For $h\in H$, twist the $S_V$-algebra structure on $\widetilde B$ by $h^{-1}$. Its completed twist is the corresponding twist of $B$, and the given action map $h$ identifies this with $B$ as an algebra. Full faithfulness in [lem-per-elkik-finite-etale-away-completion] lifts this isomorphism uniquely to the twisted model. Its inverse lifts too, so it is an isomorphism. For $h,k$, the two lifts representing $hk$ and the composite of the lifts for $h$ and $k$ agree after completion; faithfulness makes them equal. The identity lifts to the identity. This constructs the required semilinear action on $\widetilde B$ and makes the displayed completion isomorphism equivariant.

source.place: V 3.2.3: descent of the group action from the equivalence

proof.text:
Set $A=\widetilde B^H$. Since $\widetilde B$ is finite over $S_V$ and $S_V$ is finite over the Noetherian ring $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $A$ finite over $S$. Compute invariants as the kernel of $x\mapsto(hx-x)_{h\in H}$ from $\widetilde B$ to the finite product of its copies, viewed as $S$-modules. The map $S\to R$ is flat by step 3, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies
$$R\otimes_S A=(R\otimes_S\widetilde B)^H=B^H=A_0,$$
using step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] this tensor product is the maximal-ideal-of-$S$ completion of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], $A$ is a finite product of henselian local rings. The completed product is the nonzero local ring $A_0$, so it has exactly one factor: every other factor would have a nonzero residue field and hence nonzero completion. Thus $A$ is local henselian, and the completion in question is also its maximal-ideal completion by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension].

source.place: V 3.2.3: the invariant model and its completion

proof.text: The ring $A$ is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], since it is finite over the excellent ring $S$. It is Noetherian by the same excellent-ring convention [def-exc-excellent-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $A\hookrightarrow\widehat A=A_0$ and $bA_0\cap A=bA$ for $b\in A$. In particular $A$ is a domain. To check normality, write an element of its fraction field integral over $A$ as $x=a/b$. It lies in $A_0$ by normality of $A_0$; thus $a\in bA_0\cap A=bA$, and $x\in A$. We may therefore apply the excellent henselian normal-domain completion input to $A$.

For a scalar-annihilated component $Q$, $g_Q$ divides $F$ in $R$, so $g$ annihilates $A_0/Q$. By [lem-per-distinguished-polynomial-quotient], $R/(g)=D[T]/(g)$ is finite over $D$ (the classes of $1,T,\ldots,T^{\deg g-1}$ generate it). Since $A_0$ is finite over $R$, $M=A_0/Q$ is finite over $D$, hence over $A$. Let $N$ be the image of $A$ in $M$. Maximal-ideal completion gives $M=N+\mathfrak m_A M$, because $A\to A_0$ is surjective modulo $\mathfrak m_AA_0$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_A(M/N)=M/N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] to the finite $A$-module $M/N$: it is zero. Thus $A\to M$ is surjective. Put $K=\ker(A\to M)$.

Here $M$ is $\mathfrak m_D$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]. Since $g$ annihilates $M$ and is distinguished, $T$ is nilpotent on $M/\mathfrak m_D M$. Hence $M/\mathfrak m_D M$ has finite length over $S$, and a power of $\mathfrak m_S$ annihilates it. It follows that the $\mathfrak m_D$-adic and $\mathfrak m_S$-adic filtrations on $M$ are cofinal: for some $c$, $\mathfrak m_S^{cn}M\subseteq\mathfrak m_D^nM\subseteq\mathfrak m_S^nM$. The maximal-ideal topology from the finite local extension $S\to A$ is cofinal with the latter, as in [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension]. Thus $M$ is already its $\mathfrak m_A$-adic completion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] to the surjection $A\to M$: its completed kernel is $KA_0$, and its completed map is the original quotient $A_0\to A_0/Q$. Consequently $KA_0=Q$.

source.place: V 2.2.6--2.2.8 and 3.2.4: equality of the completed ideal

proof.text: In the DVR case the vertical components have the form $Q=P^{(n)}$ with $P$ height one and $\pi\in P$. Such a $P$ is minimal over $\pi A_0$: a prime strictly below it must be zero, which does not contain the nonzero element $\pi$. Apply [lem-per-vertical-symbolic-powers-completion] to $A$, $a=\pi$, and $\widehat A=A_0$. Step 7 checked excellence, henselianity and normality, and step 1 checked normality of $A_0$; $\pi$ is nonzero and lies in $\mathfrak m_A$. We obtain $P=\mathfrak p A_0$ and $\mathfrak p^{(n)}A_0=P^{(n)}=Q$. Thus this component descends as $K=\mathfrak p^{(n)}$.

For each original $I_i=\bigcap_jQ_{ij}$, let $K_i=\bigcap_jK_{ij}\subset A$, using $K=0$ for the zero component and the empty intersection $A$ for the unit ideal. Extension commutes with these finite intersections: $\bigcap_jK_{ij}$ is the kernel of $A\to\bigoplus_j A/K_{ij}$, and flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies its extension to $A_0$ with the kernel of $A_0\to\bigoplus_j A_0/Q_{ij}$. Therefore $K_iA_0=I_i$. This is equality of ideals, including their nonreduced structures.

source.place: V 2.2.1 and 3.2.4: reconstruct the original marking

proof.text: Use [lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit] for $D[T]$ at $\mathfrak q=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, obtaining a henselian local colimit $H=\varinjlim S_a$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qH$. By [lem-per-pointed-etale-limit-henselization](1), $H$ is a henselization of $D[T]_{\mathfrak q}$, so the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] gives a unique local $D[T]_{\mathfrak q}$-algebra isomorphism $H\cong S$; we regard each $S_a$ as mapping to $S$ through it. Thus $S=\varinjlim S_a$ with each $S_a$ etale of finite presentation over $D[T]$ and with a point $\mathfrak q_a$ over $\mathfrak q$ having the same residue field. Present the finite $S$-algebra $A$ by finitely many generators and relations, and each $K_i$ by finitely many elements; finiteness of these data follows from Noetherianity of $S,A$. Lift their coefficients to one stage using [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data]. This produces a finitely presented $S_a$-algebra $C_a$ and ideals $J_{i,a}$ with $C_a\otimes_{S_a}S\cong A$ carrying the ideals to $K_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-finite-ring-map] to make $C_a$ finite over a later $S_a$.

Fix this stage and write $C=C_a$, $J_i=J_{i,a}$. The map $C\to A$ takes $\mathfrak m_A$ back to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ above $\mathfrak q_a$: $C/\mathfrak n$ is an integral domain finite over the field $S_a/\mathfrak q_a=D/\mathfrak m_D$, hence is a field. In the limit, $S\otimes_{S_a}C=A$ is local. Base changing its completion gives
$$R\otimes_{S_a}C=R\otimes_S A=A_0.$$
The maximal-ideal completion of $(S_a)_{\mathfrak q_a}$ is $R$: by [lem-per-pointed-etale-limit-henselization](3), applied to the system of step 12 at the stage $a$ (which still has colimit $S$ by step 12), $(S_a)_{\mathfrak q_a}/\mathfrak q_a^n\to S/\mathfrak m_S^n$ is an isomorphism for every $n$, compatibly with the maps from $S_a$; and [lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder] identifies the maximal-ideal completion of $S$ with $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension], $R\otimes_{S_a}C$ is the product of the completions at all primes over $\mathfrak q_a$. It is nonzero local, so there is exactly one such prime and
$$\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}\cong A_0.$$
The isomorphism is induced by the specified structural maps, hence is a $D$-algebra isomorphism, and carries $J_i\widehat{C_{\mathfrak n}}$ onto $K_iA_0=I_i$.

source.place: V 2.2.7 and 3.2.4: the pointed local completion

proof.text: Finally $D[T]\to S_a$ is etale of finite presentation and $S_a\to C$ is finite. Thus $C$ is finite type over $D[T]$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $D[T]$, the fibre $S_a\otimes_{D[T]}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is etale over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product] makes it a finite product of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; tensoring the finite $S_a$-module $C$ with this fibre gives a finite-dimensional algebra over that residue field. Its spectrum is finite, with finite residue-field extensions. This proves quasi-finiteness in the stated sense. The previous step already gives finiteness of $C/\mathfrak n$ over $D/\mathfrak m_D$. All maps restrict on $D$ to the chosen invariant formal-coordinate inclusion. The construction also applies when $s=0$, and when $r=1$ the smaller coefficient ring is simply $D=\Lambda$.
